In https://github.com/bazelbuild/rules_nodejs/blob/master/packages/bazel/bazel.js#L26 we call the bazel binary using [spawnSync](https://nodejs.org/api/child_process.html#child_process_child_process_spawnsync_command_args_options). We can process and override the PATH environment variable using the options argument to `spawnSync`.

issue.title: Make powershell.exe available at build time
issue.body:
After flipping `--experimental_strict_action_env`, we need to pass `--action_env=PATH` to make sure some specific tools are available on Windows.
Fixing https://buildkite.com/bazel/bazel-at-head-plus-disabled/builds/4#a868eb9b-dc52-4ce1-8adb-0da82e8a407b

body: as a workaround, run `./node_modules/.bin/bazel` rather than `yarn bazel`

@meteorcloudy says he could look at this from a Bazel perspective after returning from vacation.

Filipe's workaround seems simple enough too, to remove this particular segment from the PATH. But it's a symptom of a larger issue of polluting the environment which we should figure out.

I can confirm that bazel cache now works with `yarn bazel` in 0.21.0. The reason is `--experimental_strict_action_env` has been switched on by default. It purges the `PATH` environment variable so that it doesn't contain the random path.

But it would still be a problem for Windows, since we added `--action_env=PATH` to make `powershell.exe` available. To fix this, we can try to remove the use of powershell.exe, it comes from https://github.com/bazelbuild/rules_webtesting/blob/c46c3f94aaee0d0a2d5bb2150d46b64bc798f0e2/web/internal/extract.bat

On the other hand, `powershell.exe` is a native tool on Windows, maybe even the strict PATH env should contain it? I'll discuss with the owner of `--experimental_strict_action_env`. BTW, this flag even broke Bazel itself, https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/7026
